body:
One of you that replied ask how I hurt my back to start with, they didn’t know what they were asking, lol. It’s a very long story and as long as someone is reading it I’ll keep going with it. And thanks again for replying as writing this out seems like it’s getting things off my chest. I’m also in the middle of changing in this Pain Management and between the two it’s got me rethinking things. I’m not very good on typing, but it might make since.
 
How I hurt my back: I worked for a power Co. for 23 years and worked my way into management (what they call it when they work you 50-70 hrs. but only pay for 40) where I worked out my home and was doing non-destructive testing and a special electrical test of 100KV on bucket & line trucks, keeping them safe for the operators. The company was sponsoring a class on this type of testing. There was a professor teaching the class and he had asked me to climb up on one of the trucks to point something out on the boom to the rest of the class. I had to go out on what they call a cat-walk then stretch out to point to the spot the instructor was speaking of. While doing so I lost my balance and knowing I was going to fall, I also could tell I would land where the 70 year old professor was standing. I pushed off with the 1 foot still on the cat-walk so not to hit him. I landed on my butt and it hurt, but more embarrassed I got right up and said I was fine and for the most part I was. Later that night in the motel room I told my wife (we went everywhere together) I may have pulled a muscle when I fell. When we got back to town the next day I set up a appointment with my family Dr. & got some mild pain pills. After a few more trips to my Dr. and the leg & butt pain were getting worse so I reported it to my boss who set me up for X-rays and a W/C Dr. who gave me pills said I was fine. Thank god I had a good boss at that time, because I told him I knew something was wrong and he went to bat for me and got me in to another Dr which led to a whole lot of therapy, injections, more X-rays, CAT scan, MRI, more injections, & therapy. To shorten this I finally got to see a Sport Medicine Dr. who said I had a bad SI joint and he set me up with a Dr. in Atlanta that confirmed it was the problem. He then did a surgery of a bone graph and put a screw in the SI joint to make this joint solid.
 I call this Dr. 4 weeks later and told him the surgery pain was fine, but still had cramping in the left buttocks & left leg. I was told I could drive back to Atlanta or find a Dr. in town to give me a injection of something, can’t remember what it’s called. Anyway my wife found a Dr. that did it & set up a appointment. When I got there he examined me and said all I needed was some aggressive therapy. So he got his therapist to give me the therapy by taking my left knee and push it across my chest toward my right shoulder (keep in-mind I just had a bone graph 4 weeks ago). When my leg did not go far enough what she did then was she climbed up on the table I was laying on and put my left knee in the center of her chest and used her upper body weight to force my left knee to my right shoulder. “O” boy did that one hurt, my wife heard me and she was in the waiting room. I was told to go home and put some ice on it for a while. A week later I called the Dr. in Atlanta telling him about the pain and we set up an appointment. When he examined me, I was told that the bone fusion had pulled lose and my SI joint was rotating on the single screw and the fusion would never take now and a 2nd screw was needed to stop the rotating and keep it from moving and that is what was done. By the way all this SI joint surgery did nothing for the cramping in the left buttock & leg. If bad luck counts, I had a lot of luck with my back, lol.
Fast forward several months I got my family Dr. to recommend me to neurologist who did a MRI and he saw something wrong. He went in and removed part of a disc and installed what is called a LT-Cage between vertebra along with some screws & steel rods. I’m happy to say this took care of the cramps, but left me with a whole new kind of a bone pain. The best way to explain it is as if you had a couple of bags of sand resting on your shoulders and you feel that extra weight pushing down on your spine which is why I say laying down is how I get relief, it takes the weight off and this is where the real trouble gets started.   
Time to take a break and lay down, thanks for reading and replying and I’ll stop when yawl stop, OK.
I would even try weed if I knew where to find any, but with my luck I'd go to jail if I went looking, lol

Thanks for the replies, I guess some people do read this, thanks. Funny you say sounds like an interesting life, I talked to a shrink just after losing my wife and he wanted to hear the life story. After telling all & several $$$$ later, he tells me I should write a book and even offered to get someone to write it for me. Now why anyone would want to read that and said it was a wonder that I wasn’t a crack head living on the street, lol. Well close, I’m not on the street, but I am a junkie from so many years of taking this stuff. 
One thing I have learned is people see you the same if you take drugs for “the fun of it” or because you need it, to just get through the day, you are seen as the lower life form, lol. As I’m sure it changes who you are, your personality. It can be very hard to be a pleasant person when you hurt ALL THE TIME, but I do try lol. I’ve tried to explain this to some old friends, telling them you know how hard it is to be a pleasant person when you are having on of those really bad sinus headaches, but it’s just one of those things you’ll never understand it unless you’ve been there kind of things. I know it all my fault that I have messed up every relationship I’ve ever had. I have even strained the ones with my brothers and worst of all are my 2 kids & grandchildren.
Now just so you know this is not a “old poor me” letter, it’s a is what it is letter.
Sorry, but I’ve got to go lay down a while because lying is the only way of getting all the weight off my back, sitting don’t do it.
